name: Bovinax
body:
Bovinaxes are a species of satyr-like bipeds that appear to be a cross between humans and aurochs, oxen, or similar, hearty bovines. As they are always quick to remind people, they are not minotaurs.

Physical

For the most part, bovinaxes have very human features. Most have long, cow-like ears and two horns reminiscent of cattle—although the size and shape of these horns varies, and some females lack them altogether. All bovinaxes have bovine legs from the knees down, including hooves for feet. They are tall and athletically built, and most would be considered quite handsome among humans—or at least among those humans who can look past their cow-like features and ignore the nagging feeling that this just might be some kind of strange minotaur after all.

Social

Bovinaxes tend to be solitary people, but kind ones. There are no major bovinax settlements, as most belong to itinerant communities or make their homes among peoples of other cultures. They resent being compared to minotaurs, whom they see as a completely distinct species that they share little in common with. A bovinax is much more likely to be found in the company of humans, elves, gnomes, halflings, firbolgs, or centaurs. They enjoy simple crafts and working with their hands, and rarely take up intellectual pursuits.

Alignment and Religion

Bovinaxes typically gravitate toward the Chaotic Good alignment, cherishing freedom and individuality above all other values. Deities of travel are popular—especially among adventurers—and those of nature, freedom, labor, and tolerance are also seen favorably.

Names

Some typical bovinax names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Bovel
Gocho
Harka
Klovit
Ongola
Rinder
Storfi
Turina
Uro
Uxa
Vila
Voush
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are robust and strong. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Con [flexible]. (2)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Sylvan. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Elven, Giant, Gnome, Orc, and Terran. (0)
Other Traits
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Natural Armor You have tough, resilient skin that provides a +1 natural armor bonus. (2)
Sprinter You gain a +10 foot species bonus to your speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions. (1)
Trample You gain Improved Overrun as a bonus feat. You do not need to meet the usual prerequisites for this feat. Any time you successfully overrun an opponent, you deal 2d4 damage + your Strength bonus. (3)
Total: 11 RP (Advanced)
Alternate Species Traits
Durable You gain Endurance as a bonus feat. You do not need to meet the usual prerequisites for this feat. This trait replaces trample.
Gore You have hefty horns that grow from the front of your head. You can use these horns to make a single gore attack. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage. This trait replaces trample.
Jumper You are exceptionally limber, and are always considered to have a running start when making Acrobatics checks to jump. This trait replaces natural armor.
Nimble You are less bulky than most bovinaxes, your body built more for agility and scouting. You gain +2 Dex, +2 Wis. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Subterranean Stride Although you will deny it to your deathbed, it’s clear you do have some minotaur blood in your family tree. While underground, you can move through natural difficult terrain at your normal speed, such as the rough stones and stalagmites of natural caverns. Any kind of worked stone or magically altered terrain affects you normally. This trait replaces sprinter.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Bloodrager Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Brawler Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or grapple attempt.
Cleric Add +1/2 to your channeled energy total when healing creatures of the fey and monstrous humanoid types.
Druid Add +1/3 to your natural armor bonus when using wild shape.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or disarm attempt.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple and +1/2 to the number of stunning attacks you can attempt per day.
Oracle Add +1/2 to your effective oracle level for the purpose of determining the effects of your curse ability.
Paladin Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using smite evil (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Ranger Add +1 hit point to your animal companion. If you ever replace your animal companion, the new animal companion gains these bonus hit points.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Acrobatics checks to jump and a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks to demoralize enemies.
Shaman Add +1/2 to your effective shaman level for the purpose of determining your spirit animal’s natural armor adjustment, Intelligence, and special abilities.
Skald Add +1 to your total number of raging song rounds per day.
Sorcerer Add one spell known from the sorcerer spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level spell you can cast.
Summoner Add +1 hit point to your eidolon.
Warpriest Add +1/2 to your channeled energy total when healing creatures of the fey and monstrous humanoid types.
Witch Add +1/2 to your effective witch level for the purpose of determining your familiar’s natural armor adjustment, Intelligence, and special abilities.
Wizard Add a +1 bonus on concentration checks made due to taking damage while casting wizard spells.
